newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to sign world information technology pact.
newsitem.headline: Israel to sign world information technology pact.

text.p: Israel intends to join the global Information Technology Agreement (ITA) but will delay reducing customs duties on certain products by an additional five years, the Industry and Trade Ministry said on Wednesday.
The ITA, which was concluded within the framework of the World Trade Organisation, calls for gradually lowering tariffs on most information-technology products to nil by the year 2000.

"The Industry Ministry said it conditioned Israel's joining that concerning certain sensitive products, such as telephone switching equipment, antennas, printed circuits and certain cables, the period for lowering rates be extended to the year 2005," the ministry said.

The ministry said the ITA would provide Israeli telecommunications and computer products duty-free access to key markets like the United States, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Indonesia and Taiwan, which have already agreed to join the pact.
The ITA is scheduled to come into force on July 1.
Israel last year had exports of $4.05 billion in communications and electronics equipment.
